message: Hi, I'm a student with a full stack certification background. My overall academic average is 79.2% in an IT/computer-science degree. I'm interested in programming and cloud computing. My family can afford at most about USD 2700 per year.
reflection_note: The initial shortlist was strong but included a program (PR0180) that is too weak in terms of career outcomes to justify its inclusion. I dropped PR0180 and swapped in PR0165, which offers an even lower cost alternative for the student to consider. All programs were checked against the hard budget constraint ($2700/year), and three high-cost options (PR0197, PR0147, PR0096) were correctly filtered out due to exceeding the maximum annual tuition.
explanation:
Halcyon Institute of Technology
This program is recommended because it aligns strongly with your career goal of programming and cloud computing, offering both "networking_cloud" and "software_engineering" fields. It fits comfortably within your budget constraint, requiring an annual tuition of $2050. Furthermore, your 79.2% grade meets the minimum requirement (70%), and you satisfy the need for a CS background. The main trade-off here is that while it offers excellent career potential with a median starting salary of $15192, there are no post-study work visa benefits listed.

Halcyon School of Engineering
This option remains relevant as it focuses on "networking_cloud," directly supporting your cloud computing goals, and its tuition ($2300) is within your maximum budget. You meet the minimum grade requirement (74%), and the program does not strictly require a CS background. The main trade-off when comparing this to other options is that while it maintains a good focus on networking/cloud, it lacks the explicit "software_engineering" component found in the Halcyon Institute of Technology listing, resulting in a lower median starting salary ($12682).

Westbrook Technical University
This program is highly recommended due to its excellent affordability, with an annual tuition of only $1700, keeping you well under your $2700 budget. It also meets your academic requirements, as your 79.2% grade exceeds the minimum (64%), and it requires a CS background which you possess. The main trade-off is that while the cost is low, this program offers the lowest median starting salary ($8729) among the three options, potentially limiting immediate earning potential.

Westbrook Institute of Technology
This option represents the most budget-friendly choice with an annual tuition of just $550, making it ideal for minimizing costs while pursuing cloud computing skills. You meet both the minimum grade requirement (54%) and the need for a CS background. The main trade-off is that this program has the lowest placement rate (59%) and the lowest median starting salary ($7845), meaning you are trading potential long-term earning power for maximum short-term cost savings.
